**SECTION C: READING COMPREHENSION**

Read the following passage carefully and answer all the questions in complete sentences. Use your own words as far as you can.

One of the greatest needs in our nation today is the fight against corruption, fraud and misappropriation of state funds. These are some of the malpractices that jeopardize the economic growth of the country, propagating stagnation and underdevelopment rather than embezzlement and misappropriation of public funds. To boost the economy and guarantee the necessary changes, the Head of State envisages that this enigmatic, bad practice has to be eradicated, or at least reduced to the barest minimum; this runs in tandem with the good governance programme.

How can this be done? This year, Transparency International (TI) placed Cameroon at the 129th position on its international corruption perception index. Dropping from an unenviable first position some couple of years ago to 129th indicates a remarkable reduction in corrupt practices in the country. However, if one considers that TI's ranking is the result of a perception of selected countries, with specific criteria taken into account, one must remain cautious. Considering the new resolve to negotiate a new economic recovery programme with the Bretton Woods Institutions, implement it, and boost the development of the country, eradicating what has contributed immensely to impediments on this path is vital.

Anti-corruption campaigns are better waged from both ends. For it is often said, and rightly too, that bribery requires givers and receivers. "It takes two to tango." The anti-corruption commission set up in almost all ministries and the coordinating structure at the Prime Ministry are expected to step up their strategies to clamp down on those who belong to either end. Obviously, the small tips for favours embraced by state functionaries must be eradicated. In fact, efforts have to be made at all levels and by the citizenry to stop the payment of colossal sums of money in bribes. That is the evil side of life. Nothing good comes easy. Notwithstanding this, what erodes the country's image more and sinks its economy into a swamp are the huge bribes dished out by contracting firms as well as the misappropriation of state revenue.

The Head of State recently ratified the UN Convention against Corruption. This should also act as a booster to the gargantuan battle against corrupt officials. Corruption, like most unethical practices, is difficult to wipe out, not because sanctions do not exist for defaulters, but because it is hard to close the lid on them. However, corrupt officials will have to understand that the dragnet for culprits has now been thrown wider through international cooperation, making it easier to catch even those who attempt fleeing across borders.

Public funds in many third world countries have been depleted and carted out by unscrupulous state functionaries, leaving the citizenry impoverished, destitute and unable to bring them to face justice.

*(From Cameroon Tribune n° 8253, 24/12/04, adapted)*

**Questions**

1) Name three ills mentioned in the text that contribute to underdevelopment in our country.

2) What is mentioned in the passage that has to go side by side with the eradication of corruption to improve the economy of the country?

3) What does the writer refer to as "both ends" when he says: "anti-corruption campaigns are better waged from both ends"?

4) Why, according to the author, is corruption difficult to eradicate?

5) Why is it possible now for corrupt officials who have fled to other countries to be brought to answer for their crimes?

**Question concernée : n°1.**

Une question de compréhension sur un texte d'opinion journalistique se répond en reformulant précisément l'argument de l'auteur, pas une impression générale sur le sujet de la corruption. Il faut distinguer les faits rapportés (le classement de Transparency International) des explications causales avancées par l'auteur (pourquoi la corruption perdure, pourquoi elle devient plus difficile à fuir).

Trois maux évoqués dans le texte comme freins au développement du pays : la corruption, la fraude et le détournement de fonds publics (l'embezzlement/misappropriation of state funds).

Cela est désormais possible grâce au renforcement de la coopération internationale, notamment depuis que le chef de l'État a ratifié la Convention des Nations Unies contre la corruption : cet accord élargit le filet (« the dragnet ») utilisé pour poursuivre les coupables, y compris ceux qui tentent de fuir en franchissant les frontières.

### Conseil
Sur un texte d'opinion journalistique, repère toujours les connecteurs de cause (« because », « for », « since ») dans le texte source : ils indiquent précisément où se trouve l'explication attendue par une question en « why », évitant de répondre par une simple reformulation du fait sans sa cause.

incertitudes: Le texte source, dégradé par un filigrane numérique entrelacé (« www.orniformation.com ») et par des artefacts de numérisation, a nécessité une reconstruction de plusieurs passages (ex. 'xhy not underdveloppment than embezzlement' reconstruit en 'propagating stagnation and underdevelopment rather than embezzlement') ; le sens général reste fidèle à l'article source cité (Cameroon Tribune, 24/12/04), mais certains détails de formulation restent des reconstructions éditoriales plutôt qu'une transcription certaine.
Aucun barème par question n'est lisible dans le document source pour cette section ; les 10 points sont donc répartis de manière égale entre les cinq questions, à titre indicatif.
